ours-block.short: Night School's attention model, taken apart for this film
ours-block.citation: media/school/block/facts.json, written by tools/school/fill_block.mjs from system/school/block.mjs: a hooked forward pass (equal to the model's own forward, bit for bit) that reads the residual stream, applies the final norm and output matrix at each depth, and knocks out heads, attention layers and MLPs by zero, mean or shuffle, or makes a sub-layer replace the stream instead of adding to it; scored on 256 held-out rows (6,144 next words, 506 copy positions).
claims: Parameters: 20864 in all; attention 8448, MLP 8384, embeddings 2240, output 1472, norms 320.

Readout at each depth (held-out loss): 2.33 from the table, 1.73 after layer 0 attention, 0.86 after layer 0 MLP, 0.75 after layer 1 attention, 0.69 at the top; copy accuracy 0.12, 0.21, 0.43, 0.82, 0.99.
Zero knockouts: layer 1 head 1 drops copy accuracy to 0.4032; layer 1 head 0 leaves it at 0.9921; layer 0 MLP raises the loss to 5.9605. On the untrained model knockouts move the loss by under 0.05.
Replace instead of add: layer 1 attention loss 6.62, layer 0 attention 4.93, layer 1 MLP 2.85, layer 0 MLP 0.69 (its output is about 10 times the stream it reads).
ours-block.n: 6,144 held-out next words (506 copy positions); one trained model; one untrained control.
ours-block.interval: No interval: one model; mean and shuffle knockouts given beside zero knockouts in facts.json.
ours-block.does_not_prove: That large models divide work the same way; a knockout shows what the model needs here, not what a part means.

vaswani2017.citation: Vaswani, A., Shazeer, N., Parmar, N., Uszkoreit, J., Jones, L., Gomez, A. N., Kaiser, L., Polosukhin, I. (2017). Attention Is All You Need. NeurIPS 30. arXiv:1706.03762.

factcheck: Independent fact-check 2026-10-15 (FACTCHECK.md): film 16 correct, 4 reword, 0 wrong; evidence 7 correct, 1 reword.
